_readme: data/wave-floors.json - the committed COVERAGE floors for the NOAA GRIB2 wave pipeline, read
by scripts/build-wave-manifest.js before waves/current.json is written.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every count gate in this pipeline is a ratio against the previous cycle
or against the oldest retained one, and a ratio cannot answer 'is this enough coverage at
all'. A cycle that resolves 40 beaches out of 16,000 passes every ratio check the moment the
cycle before it also resolved 40. The floors here are the absolute answer, and they are SEEDED
FROM A REAL CYCLE, cross-checked by a human against D1 truth, and moved only by a reviewed
commit - the same discipline data/layer-floors.json already has.
WHY IT IS KEYED BY gridsDigest. The digest is sha256 over gridsDigestInput(GRIDS) from
src/waveGrids.js: id, domain, cell size, url template, variables, cap km, water classes and
the wind-fallback flag, sorted, canonical JSON. Adding a grid, moving a domain edge, changing
a search cap, retargeting which water classes a grid accepts or flipping whether a grid's wind
plane may answer a wave-null beach changes the digest, so the new grid set has NO entry here
and the build refuses to auto-publish until someone seeds one.
The BEACH SET is deliberately not in the digest: it grows daily, and a digest that changes
daily would withhold auto-publish forever.
HOW TO SEED A NEW DIGEST.
1. Run waves.yml by workflow_dispatch with publish true. Auto-publish is withheld (an
unseeded digest and a bootstrap cycle both withhold it), so the prefix is uploaded and
readable but waves/current.json is not moved.
2. Read the produced manifest.json. Cross-check beaches.resolved against the D1 row count and
the per-grid split against where the beaches actually are before trusting any of it.
3. Commit an entry under the new digest with status "seeded", seededFromCycleId set to that
manifest cycleId, and each floor set to 0.75x the observed count (rounded down). Every
grid id in GRIDS needs its own floor: perGridFloorRefusals iterates this entry, so an
omitted grid is unfloored with no refusal and no warning.
test/waveGateData.test.js holds this file to the digest the committed GRIDS produce, but only
STRUCTURALLY: an entry exists for that digest, every GRIDS id is keyed in its grids map,
nothing is keyed that GRIDS does not contain, and the entry is wholly seeded or wholly
pending. It passes on a "bootstrap" entry by design, so a green suite is not evidence that a
grid set has been seeded. What catches an unseeded digest in production is the scheduled
withheld-publish failure in .github/workflows/waves.yml; what prevents it landing is the
sequence in docs/offline-waves.md under "Adding a grid".
SHAPE.
floors[<gridsDigest>].status               "bootstrap" | "seeded"
floors[<gridsDigest>].waveinputRecords     global floor on emitted waveinput: records
floors[<gridsDigest>].wavesRecords         global floor on emitted waves: records
floors[<gridsDigest>].grids[<gridId>]      per-grid floor on beaches resolved to that grid,
keyed by the ids in src/waveGrids.js GRIDS
A null floor means NO FLOOR HAS BEEN SEEDED YET and that check does not apply. A null is
deliberate and reviewable; an invented number is not. A floors file carrying made-up counts is
strictly worse than one carrying nulls, because a wrong floor either blocks every cycle
forever or blesses a broken one.
status "bootstrap" is NOT a licence to auto-publish. It records that the grid set is known and
its floors are still pending. Do not add a bootstrap entry for a NEW digest just to get past a
refusal - that defeats the entire purpose of keying this file by digest.

beach set, at 0.75x each measured count, rounded down. Cross-checked against D1 before commit:

mostly inner bays, sounds and estuaries the 0.16-degree grid masks; they render no wave input
rather than a wrong one, and the floors below are set against the resolved count so a cycle
that loses coast coverage refuses while one that never had it passes.
noaa_glwu keeps the floor its own first cycle seeded (1102 rows, every one resolved, median
search 0.84 km against the 10 km cap).
gridsDigest covers the GRID SET, not the beach set, so a coast that adds beaches does not
re-withhold auto-publish; re-seed by hand when the resolved counts step up materially.
